The day after the U.S. midterms, equities rallied on relief that the election results were clear-cut. But as investors digested the implications of the election results, equity markets turned sharply lower.

“In particular, the outlook for companies tied to artificial intelligence was thrown into doubt, given a wave of local ballot measures across ten states—nearly all of which backed data center restrictions—and the success of Democratic candidates who campaigned against data center expansion,” writes expert Rebecca Patterson. 

“This U.S. equity volatility has quickly spread to other asset classes and markets around the world,” she writes. “Perhaps unsurprisingly, these gyrations are fueling worries that the so-called AI bubble could soon pop.”

The volatility “is a stark reminder that politicians and policymakers should watch financial markets and economic trends, and that investors should watch politics and policy. They are all interconnected,” Patterson writes.

Read the full analysis: https://t.co/XRV88bBe8W
